title: CagA Phosphorylation Assay and Its Semiquantitative Analysis
author: Anna F. Zeitler
materials: Using the software ImageLab from Bio-Rad, set lanes and bands. Quantify signals using relative values to the control infection. Anna F. Zeitler, Luisa F. Jiménez Soto.

steps.title: Seed cells to 80‑90% confluency
steps.instruction: Seed AGS (or appropriate) cells in 6‑well plates so that at the time of infection they reach 80‑90 % confluence. For AGS cells split 1:8 after 48 h with synchronization (see step 3). Adjust seeding for other cell lines as needed.

steps.title: Prepare fresh H. pylori culture
steps.instruction: On Friday afternoon retrieve frozen H. pylori stock by scratching ice with an inoculation loop; place the loop with frozen material onto a GC‑cholesterol agar plate (10 cm diameter, ~20 ml agar) without spreading. Incubate the plate under microaerophilic conditions (10 % CO₂, 5 % O₂, 75 % N₂) at 37 °C over the weekend. On Monday passage bacteria to a fresh GC‑cholesterol plate; on Tuesday passage again to a new plate to be used on Wednesday. Optional: growth can be performed in a 10 % CO₂ incubator at 37 °C, though growth will be slower.

steps.title: Serum‑starve cells before infection
steps.instruction: Approximately 16 h before infection, aspirate the complete medium (RPMI + 10 % inactivated FCS) and replace it with serum‑free RPMI to synchronize cells in G₀. For other cell lines adjust the medium (e.g., HEK293: DMEM + serum without glutamine; immune cells may react strongly to serum deprivation).

steps.title: Harvest bacteria from plate
steps.instruction: Using a sterile cotton swab, collect all bacteria from one‑quarter of a 10 cm agar plate and place the swab into a tube containing at least 500 µl phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). Rotate the swab in the PBS with circular motions to release bacteria, minimizing liquid retained on the swab before discarding it.

steps.title: Prepare 1:100 bacterial dilution and measure OD
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µl of the bacterial suspension into 990 µl PBS to obtain a 1:100 dilution. Measure the optical density at 550 nm (OD₅₅₀) using a densitometer.

steps.title: Calculate CFU/ml from OD
steps.instruction: Multiply the measured OD₅₅₀ by the dilution factor (100) to obtain the OD₅₅₀ per milliliter of the original suspension. Approximate that an OD₅₅₀ of 0.1 corresponds to ~3 × 10⁷ CFU/ml (strain‑dependent). Verify that the calculated CFU/ml is close to this reference value.

steps.title: Determine bacterial volume for MOI 60
steps.instruction: An MOI of 60 requires 60 bacteria per cell. Assuming each well of a 6‑well plate contains ~1 × 10⁶ adherent cells at 90‑100 % confluence, add enough bacterial suspension to deliver ~6 × 10⁷ CFU per well.

steps.title: Add complete medium before infection
steps.instruction: Remove the serum‑free medium from each well and add 1 ml of complete medium (RPMI + 10 % inactivated FCS) per well 30 min prior to adding bacteria.

steps.title: Infect cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the calculated volume of bacterial suspension to each well to achieve MOI ≈ 60. Incubate the plates at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C for 3–4 h (minimum 1 h sufficient for detectable CagA phosphorylation).

steps.title: Stop infection and keep samples cold
steps.instruction: Place the plate on ice to halt infection. Keep all subsequent samples on ice, ensuring the ice surface remains free of contamination before disposal (Biosafety Level 2).

steps.title: Collect supernatant for cytokine analysis
steps.instruction: If cytokine measurement is required, collect the culture supernatant. If not, remove the supernatant with a vacuum pump, then add 1 ml PBS* (PBS containing 1 mM PMSF, 1 µM leupeptin, 1 µM pepstatin, 1 mM sodium vanadate) to each well, avoiding drying or crystal formation.

steps.title: Detach cells with scraper
steps.instruction: Using a cell scraper, gently detach cells from the well surface, moving methodically to avoid excessive scraping damage. Observe reflected light to confirm complete removal.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension to 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C in a swing‑rotor centrifuge.

steps.title: Lyse cells and prepare samples
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without losing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet in 20 µl lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors. Immediately add 25 µl 2× SDS loading buffer, boil the mixture at 95 °C for 10 min, then place tubes on ice promptly. Do not centrifuge after boiling.

steps.title: Separate proteins by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Resolve proteins using the Single‑Gel system as described by Ahn T et al. (2001).

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane using the Trans‑Blot® Turbo™ system with homemade transfer buffers. Prior to transfer, activate the membrane by briefly contacting methanol (do not use methanol with nitrocellulose membranes). Wear appropriate personal protective equipment when handling methanol.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Block the membrane in TBS‑T (20 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, 0.075 % Tween 20) containing 3 % BSA for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with anti‑phosphotyrosine antibody (clone 4G10, Millipore) diluted 1:10 000 in PBS containing 3 % BSA for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membrane after primary
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 4 times, 15 min each, with 5 ml TBS‑T (0.075 % Tween 20) at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate with anti‑mouse HRP‑conjugated antibody (Sigma) diluted 1:10 000 in TBS containing 0.075 % Tween 20 for 45 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membrane after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 4 times, 15 min each, with 5 ml TBS containing 0.075 % Tween 20 at room temperature.

steps.title: Develop chemiluminescent signal
steps.instruction: Remove all wash buffer, ensuring the membrane does not dry. Apply Millipore Immobilon Western developing solution (mix 1 ml solution A with 1 ml solution B). Roll the membrane in the solution for 1–2 min, place it between two transparencies, and detect chemiluminescence using a Gel Doc™ XR+ system.

steps.title: Quantify total protein with stain‑free
steps.instruction: Activate the gel for stain‑free detection (Bio‑Rad) to quantify total protein in each lane. Capture the stain‑free image with the Gel Doc™ XR+ and use ImageLab software to obtain normalization values.

steps.title: Normalize phosphorylation signals
steps.instruction: Using ImageLab, divide the phosphorylation signal intensity by the corresponding stain‑free total‑protein value for each lane to obtain normalized phosphorylation levels.
